cards.text: It's still the night of the Last Supper, and Jesus is still teaching His disciples. He's just told them, "Love one another." Now He turns to something harder: how the world will treat them.

cards.question: Jesus says the world may hate His disciples. Who does He say the world hated first?

cards.text: Jesus says if they belonged to the world, the world would love them as its own. It's like the group chat: post what everybody posts and you get ALL the hearts, post something different and you are LEFT. ON. READ.

cards.question: Instead, the world hates the disciples, because they are not of the world. Jesus has ___ them out of the world.

cards.text: Then Jesus reminds them of a word He spoke before: "No servant is greater than his master." When the boss gets chewed out in the big meeting, the new guy does NOT get a pass, and he just started TUESDAY.

cards.question: If people persecuted Jesus, the master, what does He say they'll do to His disciples?
Jesus also says that if people kept His word, they will keep His disciples' word as well.

cards.text: Then Jesus says people will treat the disciples like this because of His name.

cards.question: People will treat the disciples like this because of Jesus' name. What does Jesus say these people do not know?

cards.text: Then Jesus says something heavy. If He had not come and spoken to them, they would not be guilty of sin.

cards.question: Now that Jesus has come and spoken to them, they still have an excuse for their sin.
Jesus says that whoever hates Him hates someone else as well. Who?

cards.text: And it's not only His words. Jesus did works among them that no one else did.

cards.question: After seeing works no one else did, what does Jesus say these people have done?

answers.text: Seen and hated both Him and His Father
Believed in Him but kept it secret
Asked Him to show them another sign

cards.text: But Jesus says even this fulfills what is written in their Law: "They hated Me without reason."

cards.question: That line from their Law means Jesus gave them a real reason to hate Him.

cards.text: Now Jesus brings some hope. He will send them the Advocate from the Father, the Spirit of truth who proceeds from the Father.

cards.question: What does Jesus say the Advocate will do when He comes?

answers.text: Take them out of the world

cards.question: The Spirit will testify about Jesus, and Jesus says the disciples must testify too. Why?

answers.text: They have been with Him from the beginning
They know the Law better than anyone
The priests have asked them to speak

cards.text: Then Jesus stops and tells them why He's saying all this. Friend, when somebody pauses to explain WHY they're telling you something, you put the phone DOWN.

cards.question: Why does Jesus say He has told His disciples all these things?

answers.text: So they will not fall away
So they will hide from the world

cards.text: Then Jesus gets specific. They will put the disciples out of the synagogues.

cards.question: It goes further. Jesus says a time is coming when someone who kills His disciples will think he's doing what?
Jesus says they will do these things because they have not known the ___ or Him.

cards.text: Jesus says He's telling them now, so when their hour comes, they'll remember He told them. It's the friend who warns you about the pothole before you hit it, so when you hit it you go, "Oh yeah. He SAID that."

cards.question: Jesus didn't tell His disciples these things from the beginning. Why not?

answers.text: Because the Law kept Him from it

cards.text: And that's where we pause, friend. Jesus is NOT done talking to His disciples tonight, and trust me, you do not want to miss what He says next.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to guess the exact word Jesus uses (chosen vs sent vs hidden). Nothing on the earlier cards lets the baker reason toward 'chosen'. It tests wording the baker hasn't seen, not meaning.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: Card 15 quotes 'They hated Me without reason.' Card 16 then asks whether that line means Jesus gave them a real reason to hate Him. The story card right before it states the answer, so the question tests nothing.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: 'That line from their Law' points back to the quote on card 15, which is no longer on screen. The question doesn't say what the line is.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: 'Treat the disciples like this' points back to the persecution on earlier cards without saying what 'this' is.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: 'They will do these things' doesn't say who 'they' are or what 'these things' are. These are being put out of the synagogues and being killed, which were told on earlier cards that are no longer on screen.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: Several story cards are flat restatements of the verse with none of Papa Dorin's voice: stop 1 cards 8, 10, 13 and 15, and stop 2 cards 1 and 6. Only four lines across both stops carry any humor, so the walkthrough reads like a nice dad being pleasant rather than laugh-out-loud funny.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: This card is only the line saying the story isn't over. It tells nothing from John 16:4, but it cites John 16:4, which was already cited on cards 9 and 10.
findings.question: When the last story card is only the story-continues line and tells no verse, what should its "verses" field cite? Should it repeat the last verse, cite the stop's range, or be null?
